1.why: Server-side authorization enforces ownership by checking session.userId === account.id in authenticatedSession.

2.why: The same verification code can be reused for any user because the code is not tied to a specific user in the identity verification flow.

3.why: Previous sessions are not invalidated when MFA is enabled; old sessions remain active until they expire.

4.why: OTP shared secret and backup codes are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) or as salted/peppered hashes.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using node:crypto's randomBytes, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are never stored in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies; session cookies are HttpOnly.

7.why: Server-side input validation (e.g., validEmail, validPhone, validOtp) and sanitization are enforced for all user-supplied inputs.

8.why: Dynamic data is rendered via textContent in the frontend, preventing XSS from injected markup or script.

9.why: Redirects are restricted to an allow-list (only /verify-identity is permitted in signin).

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are consistently set for all responses.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are never exposed in logs, URLs, or error output; stack traces are suppressed.

13.why: Verification codes are single-use (identityCodeUsed flag) and time-bound (CODE_EXPIRY_MS).

14.why: Repeated failed attempts are rate-limited (MAX_FAILURES) and locked out (LOCKOUT_MS).

15.why: Session identifier is rotated on authentication (newSession), has idle/absolute timeouts, and is invalidated on logout.
